                Oxford Christmas Theatre in 2026
            
 
  • Blog
    •  
  • 14 Nov 2026
    •  
  • Oxford Christmas Theatre in 2026
 




  

    
Listen to audio version of this article

    
Sponsored by

  

  

    
    

    

  

  

    
0:00 / 4:42

    

      
      Instaread
    

  





December brings with it the usual bevy of Christmas theatre, from raucous panto to reimaginings of literary classics. Luckily, Daily Info is on hand to fill your stocking with some of the best holiday offerings on Oxfordshire stages this season.
  
Snow White - Oxford Playhouse
 
The Playhouse’s take on the fairest of them all has, as we’ve come to expect, a contemporary twist. Snow is up against the forces of Queen Narcissa, who plans to drain the resources of the natural world to preserve her beauty with the help of her magic mirror assistant, Miri. She’ll be joined by a cast of colourful new characters from an original script by Sarah Henley.
 
Snow White: Oxford Playhouse, Fri 20th Nov - Sun 6th Jan, timings vary. Tickets £18-51.
  
Jack and the Beanstalk - Cornerstone
 
Join Jack, Daisy the Cow and one very disgruntled giant for a journey up the beanstalk at the Cornerstone. We’ve got sets on an epic scale, a-moo-sing antics from dame Daisy and plenty of chances for the crowd to get involved - the cast will also be doing meet and greets for their performances on 19th and 20th December.
 
Jack and the Beanstalk: Cornerstone Arts Centre, Fri 18th - Wed 30th Dec, timings vary. Tickets £22-27 (concessions available).
  
A Christmas Carol Continues - The Old Fire Station
 
Years after the events of A Christmas Carol, is Ebenezer Scrooge that much of a changed man? Johnny Donahoe, creator of Every Brilliant Thing, returns to the Old Fire Station with a clever and compassionate sequel to Dickens’ classic, as Scrooge learns that real goodness is going to take a lot more work than he thought.
 
A Christmas Carol Continues: The Old Fire Station, Wed 9th - Tues 29th Dec, timings vary. Tickets £15-25.
  
Winnie and Wilbur’s Christmas Adventure - Pegasus Theatre
 
Wild Boor Ideas invites you to hop on a broomstick alongside witch Winnie and her mog Wilbur for a Christmas jaunt around the world. With puppetry and an original score, Winnie searches high and low for Wilbur’s perfect Christmas - not realising it might be closer to home…
 
Winnie and Wilbur: A Christmas Adventure: Pegasus Theatre,  Fri 11th - Thu 24th Dec, timings vary. Tickets £10-14.
  
Alice in Winter Wonderland - The North Wall Arts Centre
 
Lewis Carroll’s tale of Alice’s tumble down the rabbit hole gets a tinselly twist from Creation Theatre. Here Alice finds herself confused by Christmas’s strange traditions, and must have them explained to her by Wonderland’s whimsical residents.
 
Alice in Winter Wonderland: The North Wall Arts Centre, Sat 28th Nov - Sun 3rd Jan, timings vary. Tickets £15-37.
  
The Snow Queen - Chipping Norton Theatre
 
Young Gerda sets out on the journey of a lifetime to rescue her best friend Kai from the clutches of the Snow Queen, armed with her wits and a little help from her mum, Dame Candy Cane. Expect winter vistas, original music and something for your sweet tooth in this year’s Chippy Panto.
 
The Snow Queen: Chipping Norton Theatre, Wed 18th Nov - Sun 17th Jan, timings vary. Tickets from £18.
  
Little Robin Red Vest - Burton Taylor Studio
 
A cosy winter adventure for the younger set, based on the children’s book from Jan Fearnley. Little Robin is off to deliver cosy vests to his woodland friends to protect them from the winter chill - but what about a vest of his own? Filskit Theatre adds puppetry and Makaton to make this story leap off the page.
 
Little Robin Red Vest: Burton Taylor Studio, Wed 2nd Dec - Sun 3rd Jan, timings vary. Tickets £16 adults, £12 children.
  
Dear Santa - The Mill Arts Centre
 
The perfect gift for little Sarah can’t be hard to find, can it? Try as he might, though, Santa is stumped. In this gentle early years play for ages two and up, Santa enlists his top elf to find just the right present in time for Christmas Eve. Attendees can meet Santa after the show, with a special gift for every child.
Dear Santa: The Mill Arts Centre, Mon 14th - Thurs 24th Dec, timings vary. Tickets £18.
  
Hoppily Ever After - The Frog Prince Musical - The Story Museum
 
TransFROGrified at the hands of a sorcerer, Prince Riberto is tasked with finding the meaning of true love - and what better way than writing the perfect love song? When a royal commission comes through to his songwriting agency, it's up to Riberto and his employees, Lily and Patrick, to produce a track that's truly magical.
 
Hoppily Ever After - The Frog Prince Musical: The Story Museum, Sat 19th Dec - Fri 1st Jan. Tickets £14 per person.
